novelty_flags.label: related_work and comparator_promise_table — FreybergerRai2018UniformBands
novelty_flags.one_line: The core says Freyberger--Rai restricts attention to nonrandom translation-shaped sets and explicitly excludes randomized band selection, but the paper characterizes a general class of deterministic taut projection bands and does not make that claimed explicit exclusion; state the actual deterministic-taut scope and establish the randomized-decision gap independently.

soundness_flags.label: ass:span-compatibility
soundness_flags.one_line: Given ass:block-factor-means and rank(A)=r with A=F_pre U_D, both F_pre and U_D have rank r, so a_0=F_pre mu_0 automatically lies in col(A) and d'=f_post' U_D automatically lies in row(A); remove this redundant assumption or weaken the factor model.

soundness_flags.label: thm:global-risk-band
soundness_flags.one_line: The display sup_{P in M_n} sup_v diam C_n(v)=O_P(n^{-1/2}) has no probability law after taking a supremum over P; replace it with an explicit uniform stochastic-order quantifier, e.g. lim_M limsup_n sup_P Pr_P{sup_v sqrt(n) diam C_n(v)>M}=0.

soundness_flags.label: def:local-risk-map and prop:hinge-sanity-check
soundness_flags.one_line: The local formulas use undeclared centered objects X_0,x_0,A_0,a_00,d_0 and the hinge uses an undefined scalar a and an unspecified “before saturation” range for m; define these identities and the admissible m interval so the claimed exact benchmark is testable.

source_verification_receipts.locator: p. 119, abstract and Introduction; pp. 124–125, deterministic band construction and Theorem 3
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper characterizes a general class of taut uniform bands through projections on confidence sets and studies deterministic band endpoints/functions; it presents approximate optimization for objectives such as weighted area, rather than stating an explicit exclusion of randomized data-dependent band selection or a translation-shape-only theorem.

The paper constructs uniformly asymptotically valid confidence sets for a simplex-valued optimizer and extends the construction to a function of that weight; its result is for a population optimization problem, not a continuum-indexed moving-objective risk graph.

The paper studies sparse predictor selection in synthetic controls, establishes model-selection consistency and a faster predictor-match MSE rate, and reports post-treatment performance comparisons; it does not state simultaneous inference for a population prediction-risk graph.

source_verification_receipts.version: JASA 116 (2021), author-hosted published-paper PDF; publisher primary text access-restricted
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper develops synthetic-control prediction intervals separating fitted-weight uncertainty from an unobservable post-treatment error and includes a beta-mixing dependent-data extension; its target is a future counterfactual outcome rather than unconditional population MSE.

The paper derives analytical degrees-of-freedom/risk expressions and estimable information criteria for synthetic-control tuning, including weighting-matrix selection with covariates; it does not give an honest all-predictor population-risk band.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Rewrite the Freyberger--Rai comparison accurately: distinguish deterministic taut projection bands from externally randomized decision kernels, then state exactly which unrestricted-randomization theorem the new acceptance-subset reduction adds.
Make all local-center notation explicit and replace the global O_P display with a uniform probability statement; give the hinge's exact nonsaturation inequality for m.
Remove span compatibility as redundant under the full-rank factor parameterization, or relax the factor model so it becomes an independently meaningful identifying restriction.

Add a bridge corollary relating the fixed-ridge weight map to a named implemented synthetic-control estimator, or state the fixed-ridge target as a deliberately distinct estimator and limit the Synth/SparseSC consumer claim accordingly.
